body.x: Avatar , which made cinematic history when it was released in December 2009, shocked viewers worldwide with 3D production values that had formerly only been available at amusement park rides.

People noticed when 3D TVs, 3D monitors, 3D laptops, and other 3D-related products hit the market following the movie’s success. But while the variety of 3D equipment has increased, there are some who say that we’re still missing something that’s far more important: media content (3D movies, TV shows, etc.). A 3D industry that has not yet found a source of media is akin to a smartphone without any applications.

If you haven’t enjoyed 3D movies yet because there just isn’t enough to watch, consider trying 3D SPECTAT, a 3D converter exhibited by Cmos Media Tech at KES 2012. Taking the form of a set-top box, all you have to do is connect the device to a TV or computer monitor in your house to convert your normal 2D images to full 3D glory. We’re not just talking about movies, sit-coms, and sports on the TV, but even pictures, videos, and games on your computer, all transformed to 3D.

Using Cmos Media Tech’s proprietary algorithm, 3D SPECTAT automatically analyzes 2D images and video information and converts them into 3D in real time. The depth value of 3D videos can be automatically adjusted or controlled by the user directly. The device supports a maximum resolution of 1080p.

On the front of the device is an LED that displays the current status of the video. For example, if it says “3D-L” it means that it’s in 3D line by line mode, while “3D-S” indicates 3D side by side mode. On the reverse of the device are one HDMI output port and two HDMI input ports. On either side of the HDMI ports are a power jack and a remote jack. If you connect an IR cable to the remote jack, you can control the device easily with a remote control.
